Position anodes at the far ends and four intermediate points to ensure uniform current distribution. Use a single rectifier with optimized current distribution settings to achieve a target pipe-to-soil potential of -0.95 V at all anode locations, verified via remote monitoring of test posts installed at each anode site. The anodes shall be installed via directional drilling to a depth of 3 feet below the pipeline, ensuring no excavation of the pipeline itself.

**Expected measurable effect:**
- Stabilization of pipe-to-soil potential at **-0.95 V** (EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2026.109489]) across all monitored points, reducing current drain from coating holidays by **≥30%** (ASSUMPTION).
- Inhibition of sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) biofilm formation at defect sites, as cathodic polarization at **-0.95 V** suppresses microbial activity (EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2026.109489]).
- Formation of protective calcareous deposits at coating defects, reducing localized corrosion rates by **≥40%** (ASSUMPTION).

**How it respects constraints:**
- **No pipeline excavation:** Anodes are installed via directional drilling, avoiding direct pipeline disturbance.
- **Rectifier power budget fixed:** The intervention leverages existing rectifier capacity by redistributing current via auxiliary anodes, requiring no additional power input beyond optimized current distribution.

**Falsification test:**
